description: Itron is innovating new ways for utilities and cities to manage energy and water. We create a more resourceful world to protect essential resources for today and tomorrow. Join us. Itron Resiliency Solutions is an innovative business unit within Itron focused on solving mission critical problems for utilities through software and AI. Resiliency Solutions offers unique, market leading solutions for front-line worker safety, storm response, excavation damage prevention, construction management, and many more. These software and AI solutions solve end-to-end challenges for the utilities that power our society and are used by the largest and most complex organizations in the world such as National Grid, Southern Company, and Exelon. Itron Resiliency Solutions is a global, diverse team of builders and innovators who tackle previously impossible challenges for our customers. If you have a desire to challenge yourself, solve impactful problems, and work with a passionate and talented team, this is the place. About the role We're hiring an SDET-2 (Software Development Engineer in Test) in Bengaluru to own quality for the services our customers depend on. You'll decide what to test and how, build and maintain automation, test by hand where it finds problems fastest, and help the team ship often without breaking customers. Our India engineering team is taking full ownership of core products and growing quickly, including a ground-up rebuild of a customer-critical service. Quality is a first-class priority for us, not a phase at the end. You'll work closely with developers, Product, Customer Support and your Engineering Manager. What you'll own in your first year Own: Own quality for a service or product area end to end — test strategy, automation, release sign-off, and follow-up on escaped bugs. Test strategy. Decide what to automate, what to test by hand, and what risk is acceptable for each release. Automation that lasts. Build and extend API, UI and integration test suites that are fast, reliable and run in CI on every change. Shift left. Review designs and requirements early, and work with developers so testability is built in, not bolted on. Learn from escapes. When a bug reaches customers, find out why and close the gap so it doesn't happen again. Raise the bar. Review test code, mentor SDET-1s, and help interview candidates. What you must bring These are the bar. We can't teach them on the job. Experience: 2–5 years in software testing or development. We level on demonstrated scope, not years alone. You've built automation that runs in CI. Test suites you designed or substantially extended, that run on every change and that the team trusts. You own quality, not just test cases. You've decided what to test for a feature or release, and stood behind the call. You are comfortable testing by hand. You use manual and exploratory testing deliberately, where it finds problems faster than scripts. You work independently toward a clear goal. Given a feature or release, you plan the testing, unblock yourself, and raise risks early. Test plan Breakdown: You can take product requirements and create deep test plan including all corner cases to ensure Quality We care how you test more than which tool you did it in. Technical background You've tested production systems with a modern stack, such as: Languages: strong in at least one language such as Python, Java or JavaScript/TypeScript — you write test code with the same care as product code. Test automation: frameworks such as Pytest, JUnit/TestNG, Playwright, Cypress or Selenium, including structuring a suite so it stays maintainable. APIs and services: contract and integration testing of REST APIs, including error paths, auth and data validation. CI and cloud: running tests in CI pipelines, and testing services deployed on AWS — reading logs and metrics to diagnose failures. Databases: SQL to set up and verify data, and an understanding of how data issues show up as bugs. Non-functional testing: exposure to performance or load testing with tools such as JMeter, k6 or Locust. Exact tools matter less than depth. Strong experience on an equivalent stack is welcome. What sets great candidates apart Impact you can explain. Escaped bugs went down, release time went down, or flaky tests went away — and you can say what you did to get there. A suite you made better. You took slow or flaky automation and made it fast and trusted, not just bigger. Framework mindset: You spot repeated test code and turn it into reusable helpers, fixtures or tooling others build on. Root-cause thinking. You trace a failure to its cause in code, data or config, not just report the symptom. Product sense. You've pushed back on a release, or on a requirement that would confuse users, and been right. Lifting others. Test reviews, docs or mentoring that made developers and newer SDETs better at quality. What we look for in everyone we hire Whatever the role, we hire for six things. Customer obsession. You test the way customers actually work, and you treat every escaped bug and support ticket as a lesson. Impact over activity. You measure success by bugs that never reached customers and releases that went out smoothly, not test-case counts. Honesty. You report quality as it is, say clearly what wasn't tested, and raise release risks even when it's unwelcome. Independence. You don't wait to be told what to test. You find the risk worth covering and get it done with little hand-holding. You will work with leaders who will partner with you in the journey. Passion. Not the word on a resume — the evidence: a tool you built, a technique you went deep on, things you taught others. Depth. At least one system you've tested well enough to explain its internals, its failure modes and how you'd test them. Itron is committed to building an inclusive and diverse workforce and providing an authentic workplace experience for all employees. If you are excited about this role but your past experiences don't perfectly align with every requirement, we encourage you to apply anyway. In the end, you may be just who we are looking for! The successful candidate's starting wage will be determined based on permissible, non-discriminatory factors such as skills and experience. Itron is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. The engineering discipline bar is the same as any software role: version control, review in both directions, CI, design before implementation, and root-cause debugging by the owner. The Test Engineer will be integral part of the team and takes pride in advocating for the quality of the Zettle mobile app on Android and iOS, along with the backend and web services behind it. Meet our team: Zettle is PayPal's point-of-sale and payments product for small businesses. Zettle India is part of the Payment Services and Crypto organization, and our test engineering team supports the Zettle mobile app on Android and iOS and the services behind it. We are a centralized Test and Quality Engineering function actively moving to an automation-first, shift-left culture. Your work will reduce production defects, speed up releases, and improve the experience of small businesses that use Zettle every day. Write and merge automated cross-service / interop tests into CI/CD pipelines that gate real merges; debug every failure to root cause. Perform manual and exploratory testing on real devices, emulators, and simulators across OS versions, screen sizes, and network conditions. Test APIs and backend services using Postman or RestAssured and validate data using SQL queries. Run tests on BrowserStack and in CI/CD pipelines (Harness) and analyze failures to find the root cause. Log clear, reproducible defects in JIRA with logs (Logcat, Xcode), screenshots, and screen recordings, and follow them through to closure. Maintain test cases and test runs in TestRail, and report test status and risks to the team. Reduce flaky tests and suggest ideas to improve test coverage, speed, and quality. Hands-on experience with Espresso and/or XCUITest, with willingness to learn the other. Good Java programming fundamentals and basic knowledge of data structures. Experience with API testing (Postman, RestAssured) and writing SQL queries. Good understanding of SDLC/STLC, test design, and defect management using JIRA and TestRail. Familiarity with Jenkins, BrowserStack, and debugging tools such as Logcat and the Xcode console. Clear written and verbal communication, and the ability to work with developers and product managers. Ownership, curiosity, and a willingness to learn. Nice to have: Appium, Kotlin or Swift reading ability, mobile performance testing (Android Profiler, Xcode Instruments), JMeter, AWS, and experience in payments or FinTech.
